prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth strip supports a layered layout: the chair backs and bottle at the bottom are nearest, roughly 0.3–1 m from the camera wearer; the table and surrounding chairs are about 0.8–2 m away; and the TV, cabinet, windows, and vegetation are farther, approximately 2–8+ m away. Across all five frames, the large bright chair backs remain close and partly out of view below the frame, occluding portions of the table and more distant furniture; the bottle also remains nearby at lower right. The repeated depth structure suggests mainly a small sideways or rotational camera change rather than a strong approach or retreat, with furniture shifting laterally but staying at similar depth. This map makes foreground–background separation and occlusion order clearer than RGB, but its grayscale is not metrically calibrated, overexposed windows lose distant structure, and several boundaries around chairs, the bottle, and the table appear blended or distorted.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates nearby chairs, the bottle, potted plants, and the TV, showing their left-to-right arrangement and which silhouettes overlap: chairs occupy the lower foreground, plants and TV sit higher and farther back, and the bottle is near the lower-right edge. Across the five frames, these masks shift horizontally with the camera view; the TV remains above the chairs, while foreground chair masks change shape as different portions enter or leave the frame, indicating viewpoint rotation rather than clear approach or retreat. It makes object identity and overlap easier to see than RGB, but it supplies no trustworthy metric distance, so rough ranges must come from context: chairs and bottle about 0.3–2 m away, TV and plants roughly 2–5 m away, with the nearby chairs generally less than about 1–1.5 m from one another. The occasional “person” labels near the plants or furniture do not correspond clearly to visible people in RGB, several chair regions are merged or inconsistently split, and no reliable facing direction, gaze, or human arm-reach relationship can be inferred.
descriptions.pose: The pose maps are completely black in all five frames, so they provide no detected body or hand skeletons, facing directions, gaze cues, limb locations, or arm-reach estimates. In conjunction with RGB, this is consistent with no clearly visible person in the scene apart from the camera wearer, whose body and hands are also not visible. Because no joints appear over time, the map cannot support claims about people approaching, retreating, turning, or being occluded behind furniture. Its main spatial indication is therefore negative and unreliable: the pose detector found nothing, but that does not prove that no partly hidden or out-of-frame person exists.
